events.what: Borwein, Maitland & Skerritt lower bound of 19,908 digits on any counterexample
AI agent produces Lean proofs that A309132's primality conjecture is equivalent to Agoh–Giuga, and that for composite n, a(n) is squarefree iff n is Carmichael (Ordowski 2019 conjecture)
events.ai_basis: The proof that n is Carmichael iff n is composite and a(n) is squarefree was achieved by an autonomous AI agent, see the Tsoukalas paper and the Lean proof.

events.what: Two self-labelled speculative AI-generated Zenodo postings on the 'Arithmetic Geometry of the Giuga Condition'
events.credibility_reason: Self-disclosed as 'a creative exploration of a concept with AI — it should not be taken as correct mathematics'.

judgement.doubts: The OEIS Open results are genuine AI-generated mathematics, but about A309132's structure, not the bullet: the equivalence is a reformulation (scope none) and the Carmichael/squarefree characterisation is a different statement (variant). Neither bounds nor settles any case of the biconditional. The event field is left pointing to the OEIS Open preprint as the record's most relevant adjacent development; the status no longer rests on it. The 2013 bound predates the snapshot and is not a resolution, so open rather than open_stale.

corrections.why: F3/other: the record itself says 'Neither proof touches the truth value of Agoh-Giuga' and the core problem is 'unmoved'; a reformulation (scope none) and a squarefree/Carmichael characterisation of A309132 (variant) move no quantity on this bullet, so no event survives step 1.
F8: the AI role describes the discarded A309132 event; with nothing surviving there is no event carrying an AI role. The basis quote is kept as evidence of the adjacent result.
F14: 'confirmed' on a row where nothing on the bullet was settled; open carries null.
other: the record reports no post-snapshot proof, refutation or bound improvement on the biconditional itself.
